reference.title: Close Grip Push-up
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: More reps, then slower lowering, then feet elevated or a weighted vest

cues.text: High plank with the hands under the chest, closer than shoulder width (index fingers about a hand apart), body in one line.
Breathe in and lower with the elbows brushing back along the ribs.
Chest just above the hands, elbows pointing back toward the feet.
Breathe out and push through the palms until the arms are straight.
Lock in the plank at the top and go again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tight to the ribs, pointing back toward the feet.

mistakes.mistake: Hands too far forward (under the face)
mistakes.fix: Place the hands under the lower chest so the forearms stay close to vertical at the bottom.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes.
Lower until the chest is close to the hands.
Turn the fingers slightly out or widen the hands a little.

kinematics.norm: Inside shoulder width; 50% of shoulder width raised triceps activity versus 100% and 150% (Kim 2016); diamond hands (thumbs and index fingers touching) gave the highest activation (Intziegianni 2026)
Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows bend to about 90 degrees or more at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Elbows close to the ribs, about 10-25 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Head, trunk, hips and ankles in one straight line throughout (clinical opinion)
Palms flat; the wrist bends back about 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up; lab studies used 2-2.5 s per repetition (Marcolin 2015)

sources.title: GymVisual #025912, Close Grip Push-up, video (movement reference)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

Marcolin, Petrone, Moro, Battaglia, Bianco and Paoli 2015, selective activation of shoulder, trunk and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants (J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132)
Intziegianni, Katsamis, Michaelides and Parpa 2026, electromyographic activation of the pectoralis major and triceps brachii during standard, diamond and wide hand position push-ups (Muscles 5(1):18)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: keep the elbows tucked rather than flared out to the sides, and shorten the range if needed (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Elbow pain: narrow hands put more load through the elbows; widen the hands a little or regress to an incline (clinical opinion).
modify: Wrist or elbow discomfort: hands slightly wider, or hold hex dumbbells.
Too hard: hands on a bench (incline close-grip push-up) or knees down.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Still a main pusher: pectoralis activity was higher with hands at or inside shoulder width than at 150% (Kim 2016) and highest with diamond hands (Intziegianni 2026).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Still a main pusher: pectoralis activity was higher with hands at or inside shoulder width than at 150% (Kim 2016) and highest with diamond hands (Intziegianni 2026).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main target: narrowing the hands raised triceps activity versus shoulder-width and wide push-ups (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015), and diamond hands gave the highest relative triceps and chest activation in Intziegianni 2026.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main target: narrowing the hands raised triceps activity versus shoulder-width and wide push-ups (Kim 2016; Marcolin 2015), and diamond hands gave the highest relative triceps and chest activation in Intziegianni 2026.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage and spreads them at the top.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades on the rib cage and spreads them at the top.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the hips from sagging or piking: the body moves as one plank.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.

guides.label: Elbows travel back along the ribs
